\nopagebreak\noindent Production law: Schubert et al. (Garofalo (hyperbolic sine)~\cite{Schubert2003ECTC}), for SnAgCu (near-eutectic SAC); applied to SAC305 in the citing literature; the joint is SAC305 (BGA). The solver integrates $\dot\varepsilon_{\mathrm{in}} = A(T)\,(\sigma_{\mathrm{vm}}-\sigma_y)^{n(T)}$ with a zero yield surface ($\sigma_y = 10^{-6}$~MPa), i.e., the applied von~Mises stress the laws were fitted in, with no rate-independent hardening; the law enters as a temperature-dependent Norton surrogate fitted at every 2.5-$^\circ$C row of the card (listed at 25-$^\circ$C steps) over the stress window the joints visit, 10.4--35.9~MPa hot, 17.3--50.4~MPa cold (converged); surrogate rate error at most 15\,\% (hot dwell) and 23\,\% (cold dwell). Elasticity: $E(T) = 45 - 0.12\,(T-25)$~GPa (floor 5~GPa), $\nu$ = 0.36 (room-temperature $E$ from~\cite{Paska2024SAC305}; slope and $\nu$ assumed); thermal expansion 21.5~ppm/K, stress-free at 25\,$^\circ$C.\par
\endgroup

\noindent\emph{Limitations of the solder laws.}
\begin{itemize}
\item The production law (Schubert et al.) was fitted to SnAgCu (near-eutectic SAC); applied to SAC305 in the citing literature, not to the joint's SAC305 (BGA).
\item Its constants are reprinted without their data window, so its calibration window is not stated; inside the measured window of the band laws its creep rate is 13--73 times the measured Sn3.9Ag0.6Cu rates (geometric mean 40).
\item The band law Xiao and Armstrong (Sn3.9Ag0.6Cu (not SAC305)) is calibrated on 45--150\,$^\circ$C, 7.51--15.92~MPa; the joints visit 15--32.6~MPa hot, 18.3--40.2~MPa cold, which extrapolates stress 15--40.2~MPa visited against 7.51--15.92~MPa; the 25-$^\circ$C cold dwell (rows below 45\,$^\circ$C).
\item The band law measured Norton fits (Sn3.9Ag0.6Cu (not SAC305)) is calibrated on 45--150\,$^\circ$C, 7.51--15.92~MPa; the joints visit 15.7--46.7~MPa hot, 26.1--70.5~MPa cold, which extrapolates stress 15.7--70.5~MPa visited against 7.51--15.92~MPa; the 25-$^\circ$C cold dwell (rows below 45\,$^\circ$C).
\item The Norton surrogate reproduces the production law within 15\,\% (hot dwell) and 23\,\% (cold dwell) in rate over the visited window; the error travels with the card.
\item Every compared local response is recomputed under each law of the band; the rankings hold across the laws.
\end{itemize}

\nopagebreak\noindent Critical joint under the full cut-boundary displacement: the maximum response over the BGA lattice, production law at its converged window. Lattice: legal sites of the 0.8-mm lattice (Z2: the ring around the board opening), every one with its own kinematics from the case's converged fields. Base: the top 30 by $|\Delta u_{xy}|$, by relative face tilt, by $|\varepsilon_z|$ and by the deforming $\Delta u$, the strict Pareto front in ($|\Delta u_{xy}|$, $T$) and the corners; front: the lattice's Pareto front in the screening features (deforming $\Delta u$, $|\Delta u_z|$, $T$). The response is not monotone in ($|\Delta u_{xy}|$, $T$) (violations: reversed / all dominance pairs of the solved sites, largest excess), but is in the screening features within the margin (reversals beyond 1\,\% / pairs, largest): a site dominated in them by a solved site $c$ responds at most (1 + margin)$\,\deps(c)$, margin = max(10\,\%, twice the largest reversal). Every lattice site whose bound exceeded the maximum found was solved, until none did (closed for every case): the maximum-response site bounds the whole lattice. Ratio: its response over that at the maximum-$|\Delta u_{xy}|$ site. The other laws of the band are screened the same way at their own windows (Xiao and Armstrong: 1051 sites solved, measured Norton fits: 1049 sites solved); their maximum-response sites are the production law's.\par

Production mesh: graded $h_{xy}=1.1$~mm grid with every in-plane interval split in two (r21); 8-node hexahedra (thermal C3D8, structural C3D8I incompatible modes); CalculiX~2.23. Thermal: steady conduction, direct solver; E--T stop: every coupled region temperature changes by less than 0.25~K and the loss by less than 0.1\,\%; coolant energy balance iterated to 0.02~K. Structural: linear thermoelastic, $T_{\mathrm{ref}}=25\,^\circ$C, rigid-body motion restrained only, iterative Cholesky solver (verified against the direct SPOOLES solver, Table~\ref{tab:supp-verif}). Machine: two-socket Intel Xeon Gold 6342 (2.8~GHz, 48 cores), shared; thermal solves on two threads, structural on one. Times include every E--T iteration (each a thermal solve with its coolant balance) and the structural solve with the all-site joint search; they exclude geometry construction and meshing (under 2~min per integration), the local solder model and postprocessing. Sensitivity variants use the same chain. Peak memory: the largest resident set of any process (thermal and structural solves of the case); other stages: the coarsest mesh rung (r11) 0.5~GB; the through-thickness rung (r12) 1.0~GB; the finest rung (r31) 27.3--32.2~GB; the complete-package MOOSE reference 4.7~GB; the mechanics-only solutions on converged fields 0.8--1.6~GB; the reflow and bonding checks 0.9--2.4~GB; a critical-joint search of the local model 0.1--0.4~GB; the local-model checks with the finest joint mesh 2.7~GB.\par
\endgroup

\nopagebreak\noindent One rule for every comparison: $D = y_b - y_a$ is resolved when $|D+\beta_D| > U_{95}(D)$, with $\beta_D$ the signed production-mesh bias and $U_{95}(D)$ the uncertainty of the difference at about 95\,\% coverage. Discretization: a GCI-type estimate on the nested ladder r11/r21/r31 of $D$ itself (the observed order with $F_s = 1.25$ where the ladder is asymptotic, $|p - 2| \leq 0.2$; otherwise $F_s = 3$ with the order limited to [0.5, 2]), so errors shared on one mesh family cancel only where they move together; the through-thickness split r11$\to$r12 ($F_s = 3$), the E--T stop of each case and the matched-reference agreement of the solver, in quadrature. Columns: the components of each integration's ideal-decoupling reference ladder (cooling~A production case), relative to the value (temperatures: to the rise above the inlet); $U_{95}$ of each compared case. $\deps$: own local numerical $U$ (L0$\to$L3, cycle count), resolved only when resolved under every law of the solder-law band. Model-form uncertainty is not part of $U$: it is covered by solving both integrations under each declared alternative (Table~\ref{tab:supp-variants}). Comparisons, lower integration first (R: resolved; --: not resolved; P: pending): Cooling~A, Z1/Z2: Loss Z2 R; Peak temp.\ Z1 R; Die warpage Z1 R; $\du$ Z1 R; $\deps$ Z2 R. Cooling~A, Z1/Z3: Loss Z1 R; Peak temp.\ Z1 R; Die warpage Z1 R; $\du$ Z1 R; $\deps$ Z3 R. Cooling~B, Z2/Z1: Loss Z2 R; Peak temp.\ Z2 R; Die warpage Z1 R; $\du$ Z1 R; $\deps$ Z2 R. Cases: integration, cooling (A: top plate; B: top plate and bottom plate, the bottom one behind a 50-\textmu m TIM) and input state when not the production state (implemented decoupling): ideal, ideal decoupling; bare, bare decoupling; ratio pulse, a square pulse at the overall conversion ratio; Z3 always with the coupled land-side redistribution. A check that fails only on the whole-field bound is unresolved; such a candidate is not ranked either.\par
